## Samsung Blocks Smart TV Apps That Covertly Share Users' Internet Connections

Samsung's proactive privacy enforcement in smart TV signals a shift toward privacy-forward consumer product positioning — this could pressure third-party ad-tech or data-broker players reliant on smart TV behavioral data and may influence competitive dynamics in the connected-device ecosystem.

- Samsung is actively blocking Smart TV applications that secretly share users' internet connections with third parties.
- The action is framed as a privacy and security enforcement measure; no regulatory mandate is cited, indicating a voluntary product decision.
- Coverage appears in international outlets, suggesting the policy applies broadly across markets.
- No impacted third-party app names or data-sharing partners are identified in the available headlines.
